at-0001.title: Round money only with round_money
at-0001.content: Round monetary results only via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

last_failure.review_comment: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

at-0002.title: Normalize money via to_money and round_money
at-0002.content: Always pass monetary values through to_money() and round_money() from ledgerly.money before storing or comparing them; compare against ZERO rather than a literal Decimal.

at-0003.content: Reject invalid input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors with stable snake_case codes such as invalid_state, invalid_quantity and negative_amount.

at-0004.title: Reject bools and non-int quantities
at-0004.content: When validating integer quantities, explicitly exclude bool (isinstance(quantity, bool)) because True/False are ints in Python, and require isinstance(quantity, int).
